title: Static and dynamic errors in feedback systems

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Feedback makes the closed-loop gain approach \(1/f\), but never exactly. The **static error** at DC is set by the DC loop gain \(T_0\): the actual gain is short of ideal by the fraction \(1/(1 + T_0)\).

The **dynamic error** comes from the loop gain falling with frequency. Above the op-amp's dominant pole, \(|T(j\omega)|\) drops by 20 dB/decade, so the error grows. In time, the same limited bandwidth shows up as a finite settling time for a step: the output approaches its final value exponentially with the closed-loop time constant.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ \frac{A_{CL}}{1/f} = \frac{T}{1 + T}, \qquad \varepsilon = \frac{1}{1 + T} \]
Static error: \(\varepsilon_0 = \dfrac{1}{1 + T_0}\).
Single-pole loop gain: \(T(j\omega) = \dfrac{T_0}{1 + j\omega/\omega_p}\)
Closed-loop step: \(\tau_{CL} \approx \dfrac{1}{f\,\omega_u}\), settling to within \(\varepsilon\) takes \(\tau_{CL}\ln(1/\varepsilon)\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
A loop has \(T_0 = 250\), so the static error is \(1/251 \approx 0.4\%\). The loop pole is at \(\omega_p = 200\ \mathrm{rad/s}\). At \(\omega = 2\times10^{4}\ \mathrm{rad/s}\):
\[ T \approx \frac{250}{1 + j100} \approx -j2.5, \quad |1 + T| = \sqrt{1 + 6.25} \approx 2.69 \]
The error grows to about \(1/2.69 \approx 37\%\). Fine at DC, poor at that frequency.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Using the DC loop gain at all frequencies.
- Forgetting the complex addition in \(1 + T\).
- Settling-time slips: settling to 0.1% takes about \(6.9\tau\), not \(3\tau\).
- Confusing open-loop pole with closed-loop bandwidth.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: These errors set how much open-loop gain and bandwidth you need for a given precision. They connect to datasheet specs such as open-loop gain and GBW.
